raw_expected_statement: For the source construction with integers 3 <= n <= d, k = floor(d/n), kappa >= 4, sign-conditioned Haar single-block Gaussian mixtures P_b, and the actual averaged full target laws bar_pi_b of Eq. (6), the Hellinger affinity of bar_pi_+1 and bar_pi_-1 equals the kth power of the Hellinger affinity a of P_+1 and P_-1. In the source density notation: integral_{R^d} sqrt(bar_p_+(x) bar_p_-(x)) dx = (integral_{R^n} sqrt(p_+(y) p_-(y)) dy)^k = a^k. This applies both when kn < d, using the normalized common residual standard Gaussian, and when kn = d, omitting that factor.

objects.expectation: The operands are the actual averaged target measures of the hard Gaussian family, not arbitrary functions introduced only by normalization conditions.
details: O(n) is the real orthogonal group with Haar probability; mu_{n,b} is that probability conditioned on det O = b, b in {-1,+1}; each component has full-Haar probability 1/2.
A_O = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4) (O + O^T). The covariance is A_O^{-1}, not A_O.
P_b = E_{O~mu_{n,b}}[N(0,A_O^{-1})] is the single-block mixture law. The source writes p_b for its density. P_b need not itself be Gaussian.
For each fixed b, O_1,...,O_k are independent with law mu_{n,b}. They share one fixed determinant sign; signs are not independently randomized block by block.
A_boldO = diag(A_O1,...,A_Ok,I_{d-kn}), D_b is its law, pi_A = N(0,A^{-1}), and bar_pi_b = E_{A~D_b}[pi_A]. Eq. (6) identifies this actual averaged law with P_b^{tensor k} tensor N(0,I_{d-kn}).
bar_p_b is a density of that bar_pi_b, and a is exactly the single-block affinity in A2.Ex68. A scalar named affinity without its actual-law identification is insufficient.

domains.expectation: Finite-dimensional Euclidean Borel probability laws, with source density integrals taken against Lebesgue measure and with the block coordinate decomposition explicitly justified.
details: d and n are integers, 3 <= n <= d, k = floor(d/n), and r = d-kn is a nonnegative integer satisfying r < n. In this source domain k >= 1.
Each x_j lies in R^n; for kn < d the residual z lies in R^r with r > 0; the combined source coordinate x lies in R^d.
There is no source branch kn > d. Natural-number subtraction alone must not silently assign semantics to this invalid source branch.
A generic theorem on finite products or arbitrary k may be useful, but the source-facing specialization must recover the admissible source d,n,k relation and actual R^d law.
A zero-dimensional residual law can encode the omitted-factor endpoint only if its unit-mass semantics and its identification with the source omission are established.

quantifiers.expectation: The equality holds for every admissible source parameter choice, simultaneously identifying the +1 and -1 averaged laws at that choice.
details: Choose admissible d,n,kappa; define k and the source laws; then the displayed affinity equality holds. The identity is not existential in the source laws or their densities.
Within each sign-conditioned prior the k blocks are independent and identically distributed; the comparison is between the two resulting product laws.
Density representatives may be chosen, but the conclusion must be invariant under changing them on the relevant reference-measure null sets.
The source's later choice n = 2T+1 is a main-theorem application, not an additional hypothesis of the tensorization identity. T and epsilon do not occur in this target equality.

assumptions.expectation: Public mathematical hypotheses come from the source standing construction and typing. Probability, domination, measurability, density factorization and normalization needed by the proof must be justified from the laws or reused as proved dependencies, rather than accepted as new public estimates.
details: STANDING: n >= 3 and kappa >= 4 in B.2; n <= d and k = floor(d/n) from the hard-family construction; d >= 1 from S2.
STANDING/definition: sign-conditioned Haar probability and independent draws for each fixed b.
TYPING: Euclidean/Borel measurable spaces and finite block indices implicit in the source notation.

The raw source invokes Eq. (6), Tonelli and integral phi_r = 1. It does not introduce new public premises asserting Ex70, Ex71, product-RN formulas, density integrability, unit mass, or the final affinity equality.

Positive definiteness, Gaussian existence and normalization, mixture well-definedness, absolute continuity, and measurable density versions are internal obligations of the source construction; a theorem-shaped assumption supplying any of these must be checked for source-predicate smuggling.
The inequality a <= exp{-(1/8)exp(-10n/sqrt(kappa))} is not required to prove exact tensorization. Its use belongs to the downstream Ex72 bound.

conclusion.expectation: Exact equality Aff(bar_pi_+,bar_pi_-) = Aff(P_+,P_-)^k = a^k, not merely an inequality, a definition unfolding on arbitrary product densities, or a bound on an unrelated numerical surrogate.
details: For kn < d the source's middle expression is the product of k single-block affinity integrals multiplied by integral phi_r; the latter factor is exactly one.
For kn = d the same exact equality holds after omitting the residual factor.
A measure/Radon-Nikodym statement is an acceptable formulation only if it denotes this actual-law Hellinger affinity and is shown equivalent to the source Lebesgue-density integral.
The reader must be able to apply the equality in the source downstream step TV(bar_pi_+,bar_pi_-) >= 1-a^k. The final numerical TV lower bound remains outside this one target.

scopes_senses.expectation: Ordinary Hellinger affinity, not squared Hellinger distance, total variation, a per-instance Gaussian comparison, or an affinity computed before averaging.
details: Aff(P,Q) = integral sqrt(p q) d lambda, with no prefactor 1/2 and no outer square; for probability laws its value is in [0,1].
The order is first average the Gaussian laws under each sign prior, then take affinity. It is not E affinity(pi_A,pi_B), nor the average of per-matrix affinities.

The source's p_b and bar_p_b are Lebesgue densities. A RN implementation is a quotient/representative object: equality of densities is a.e.; equality of integrals/affinities must be representative independent.

If the reference measure is changed from Lebesgue to another common dominating measure, reference-measure invariance must be supplied rather than silently assuming product factorization for an arbitrary dominating measure.
The common residual factor contributes integral sqrt(phi_r phi_r) = integral phi_r = 1 by nonnegativity and normalization. Its cancellation uses the same residual law under both signs.

Eq. (6) is equality of probability laws. Passing from that law equality to Ex70 is an identification of density versions and coordinate measures, not a pointwise equality of arbitrary RN representatives.
The identity is exact real-number equality. Any extended-nonnegative integral or RN toReal conversion must retain finiteness and the intended real value.

constant_dependencies.expectation: The tensorization exponent is exactly the source integer k. No numerical constant, loss factor, or extra dimension/covariance dependence enters the equality.
details: d,n,kappa determine the source construction; k = floor(d/n); a depends on n and kappa through the sign-conditioned Gaussian mixtures.
The common residual law has affinity exactly one independently of residual dimension.
The constants 1/8 and 10 belong to Eq. (25) and the last line of Ex72, not to Ex71 itself.
The generic multiplicativity mechanism does not require kappa-dependent estimates, even though the source laws are defined using kappa.

measure_representative_normalization_con: Identify the actual centered Gaussian N(0,A_O^{-1}) and the averaged measures; positive-definite precision must give the intended normalized Gaussian rather than a default/fallback object on invalid inputs.
Identify the Borel probability mixture kernel and sign-conditioned Haar probabilities, and show its averaging operation is the source P_b and bar_pi_b.
For source volume integrals, densities are measurable nonnegative functions with integral one and are RN derivatives a.e. of the actual laws with respect to Euclidean Lebesgue volume.
Prove or reuse absolute continuity of actual mixture laws with respect to volume; merely postulating a normalized function called a Gaussian-mixture density does not identify a probability law.

Any finite-product RN-density factorization is an a.e. statement for the product reference measure; lift component a.e. equalities correctly to the finite product before multiplying or taking square roots.

If source R^d and a finite-product Euclidean carrier are different formal types, identify the actual coordinate rearrangement, measurable equivalence and Lebesgue pushforward/product measure. A dimension count by itself is not an equality of measures.

Justify square-root multiplication for nonnegative factors, measurable nonnegative integrands for Tonelli, and the resulting finite real affinity value. A probability domination argument may discharge finiteness internally.
Show affinity is insensitive to density representatives and, if used, to the selected common dominating reference measure.

For r > 0 the residual standard Gaussian density has unit volume integral. For r = 0 either omit it as the source does or prove that the chosen zero-dimensional representation contributes exactly unit mass.

raw_source_proof_topology_expectations.status: Independent expectation only; not an approval or duplicate of another actor's source graph.
target_route: S2 fixes actual Gaussian target pi_A and probability/density conventions.
S3.E4 and S3.E5 define the actual precision matrices; S3.SS1.p2.1 defines independent block priors at one fixed sign.
S3.E6 identifies the average target as the product of k identical block mixture laws and the common residual Gaussian, with its explicit endpoint omission.
A2.SS2.p2.1 identifies p_b as the density of P_b; A2.Ex68 defines a as the single-block affinity.
A2.Ex70 translates Eq. (6) to a product density for bar_pi_b on block-plus-residual coordinates.
For kn < d, nonnegative factor algebra, Tonelli and normalization of phi_{d-kn} yield the middle line of Ex71; identical block factors and Ex68 give a^k.
For kn = d, the separate omitted-residual route yields the same equality.
A2.Ex72 consumes this exact equality through TV = 1 - integral min >= 1 - full affinity = 1-a^k. The subsequent exponential bound uses Eq. (25), a separate input.
